summary: Wave 34 admin-lane security determination for the `auth-identity` code-drift cluster (9 objects, 64 tsc hits): verification_requests, verification_documents, verification_badges, verification_criteria, verification_history, calculate_verification_score, channel_participants, get_verification_status, submit_verification_request. The admin lane could not repair these because every consumer file is outside the admin file ownership for this wave — 7 of 9 objects have lib/services/verification.service.ts as their only consumer, and lib/services/** is owned by the design-system lane, which also owns the orphaned shared pile this wave. The determination below is the required fail-closed/fail-open classification, proved per object against executable source. Headline: NONE of these objects is a live identity or verification surface, and 8 of 9 fail closed at runtime. One is a genuine silent-wrong-state defect.
working_set: lib/services/verification.service.ts — sole consumer of 8 of the 9 objects; class VerificationService, singleton verificationService at line 535
lib/services/project-workspace.service.ts:488 — the only silent-wrong-state consumer of channel_participants
lib/supabase/optimized-client.ts:319 — the other channel_participants consumer, and it also embeds profiles!sender_id(display_name)
components/verification/account-verification.tsx — the only importer of verification.service.ts, and itself unreachable

risk_determination.evidence: Each RPC call destructures `{ data, error }` and the very next statement is `if (error) throw error` (verified at lines 87-88, 103-104, and the same pattern for the score RPC). The routine is `getStateSigningSecret`-style fail-fast, not a default. PostgREST returns an error for an unknown function, so the throw fires and nothing is returned to a caller as a verified value.

Every table read follows the same `if (error) throw error` guard. Confirmed by a scoped tsc run over the file: all five names appear only as the first argument to `.from(...)` and each is rejected by the generated `Database` union (SelectQueryError / TS2345), never as a tolerated optional.

risk_determination.risk: fail-closed, but the whole channel-listing query is broken
risk_determination.evidence: The query selects `channel_participants` with an embedded `channel:communication_channels(... sender:profiles!sender_id(display_name))`. A nonexistent base table makes PostgREST reject the whole statement, and `getUserChannels` returns the raw result object, so the error propagates to the caller. No partial or unfiltered channel list can be returned. Note this consumer ALSO carries the Wave 34 `admin` cluster drift: `profiles.display_name` does not exist, which independently invalidates the embedded sender projection even if the base table were restored.

risk_determination.risk: SILENT WRONG STATE — the only genuine defect in the cluster
risk_determination.evidence: The insert is `await supabase.from('channel_participants').insert({...})` with NO destructured `error` and no check of any kind. The statement is awaited, its result is discarded, and execution continues into `this.logActivity(...)`. Because the table does not exist, the insert always fails silently, so `acceptInvitation` resolves successfully, the collaborator is accepted into the project, an activity row is written claiming the join succeeded, and the user is NEVER enrolled in the project communication channel. This is a silent-wrong-state authorization-adjacent gap, not a fail-open: the collaborator does gain project access they were granted, but they silently lose the channel that carries the project's communications. Required fix: destructure and check the error, and decide with the product owner whether acceptance should abort or record a partial state. Because the write is a bare `eq`-less insert with no org predicate, also confirm the surrounding `acceptInvitation` authorization before enabling it.

liveness_determination.finding: The whole verification surface is a retired, unreachable island. It is NOT a live identity surface and there is no credential-bearing verification path to protect.
evidence: lib/services/verification.service.ts has exactly ONE importer in the entire repository: components/verification/account-verification.tsx:5. Verified with a repo-wide search for the module path, the `verificationService` symbol, and the component name; there are no dynamic imports, no barrel re-export and no route reference.

components/verification/account-verification.tsx itself has ZERO importers. A search for `account-verification` and `AccountVerification` across the repository returns only the file itself plus two documentation rows (docs/implementation/ui-ux-completion/CANONICAL_COMPONENT_REGISTER.csv and docs/engineering/generated/components.md).

The one live verification surfaces in the product read DIFFERENT columns on DIFFERENT tables: artist_profiles.verification_status, venue_profiles.verification_status, profiles.is_verified, and lib/admin/workforce-credentials.ts's own `verification_status` enum for workforce credentials. None of them references a verification_* table or RPC. lib/venue/**, lib/artist/**, contexts/artist-context.tsx and app/artist/** are outside the admin working set and were not modified.

The drift therefore cannot be a fail-open identity risk: no request path can reach it. The only data the rule could reach is the deterministic fixture material in the integrations test file, and even that is not in this cluster.

Correction to the database lane's inventory: it lists lib/services/venue.service.ts as a live consumer of submit_verification_request. That is wrong. A scoped tsc over the file and a repo-wide search show venue.service.ts references only `verification_status` at line 213, which is a venue_profiles column on a different surface. There is no submit_verification_request call in that file.
liveness_determination.consequence: The correct disposition is deletion of the unreachable island, not resurrection of the schema. Re-creating verification_* tables would revive a retired credential-adjacent surface with no owner, no reviewer and no RLS story, which is strictly worse than the current unreachable-and-erroring state.

recommended_disposition: lib/services/verification.service.ts and components/verification/account-verification.tsx: delete both as a unit. They are an orphaned island, they are the sole consumers of 8 of the 9 drifted objects, and deleting them retires the cluster without a migration. If the product wants a verification surface again, it should be built on artist_profiles.verification_status / venue_profiles.verification_status, which already exist in the active chain.

lib/services/project-workspace.service.ts:488: fix the discarded error (this is a real bug independent of the drift), then repoint the channel enrollment to whatever the canonical membership table is. `channel_participants` is created only in supabase/migrations_backup/20250200000000_communication_system_foundation.sql, which is out of chain. The design-system lane owns lib/services/** and must confirm the live membership table before repointing; the admin lane did not guess one because no canonical destination is recorded anywhere in the repository.

lib/supabase/optimized-client.ts:319: repoint to the same canonical membership table and drop `profiles.display_name` from the embedded sender projection in favour of `profiles.full_name`. Note lib/supabase/** is not admin-owned, so the admin lane did not touch it; it is listed here because it is the second half of the channel_participants object and the two halves must be fixed together.
Do NOT author a migration for any of these nine objects. The database lane's own basis text says re-creating them 'would resurrect a retired surface'.
